# Task 041 shared whitespace-visible COLLAPSE conformance corpus.
#
# ONE canonical corpus drives the Rust, C++, and Ada generated validators, so
# the three backends are proven to agree rather than each passing its own
# curated subset. Rust-side tests read this file and emit the cases into the
# probe program for every language.
#
# THIS FILE IS THE COLLAPSE HALF ONLY.
# The preserve half lives in whitespace-visible-preserve.txt and has DIFFERENT
# expectations for the same inputs. Do not merge the two: an input such as
# "  a   b  " is stored as "a b" here and as "  a   b  " there. Keeping them in
# separate files is what prevents one policy's expectations from being copied
# onto the other.
#
# FORMAT
#   '#' begins a comment line; blank lines are ignored.
#   VALID <input> => <expected stored form>
#   INVALID <input>
# Exactly one space follows the VALID/INVALID keyword.
# <input> is escaped so whitespace and control cases are unambiguous:
#   \s space   \t tab   \n line feed   \r carriage return   \\ backslash
#   \u{HEX} any code point
#   <empty> the EMPTY field, as a whole field only.
#
# THE <empty> TOKEN
# The shared loader trims each line's end before splitting on ' => ', so an
# empty field cannot be written as literal nothing, and trailing-space padding
# would be removed by the same trim. `<empty>` is the explicit spelling. It is
# load-bearing here: this profile's minLength is 0, so the empty string is a
# VALID value, and whitespace-only input NORMALIZES to it.
#
#   Some("") = construction succeeded, stored value is the empty String
#   None     = rejected
# An empty stored value is NOT a NUL character and NOT missing data.
#
# AUTHORITY
# Read verbatim from the pinned UCI 2.5 release bytes:
#   UCI 2.5 093610b7753944059360d3236770ab446d039556
#           UCI_SecurityMarkings_v2_5_0.xsd:8565 (1024)
#           UCI_SecurityMarkings_v2_5_0.xsd:8576 (4096)
#
#   <xs:restriction base="xs:string">
#     <xs:minLength value="0"/>
#     <xs:maxLength value="1024"/>
#     <xs:whiteSpace value="collapse"/>
#     <xs:pattern value="[&#x20;-&#x7E;\n\r]{0,1024}"/>
#   </xs:restriction>
#
# UCI 2.6 does NOT carry this shape: it drops the whiteSpace facet and raises
# minLength to 1. That release's expectations are in the preserve corpus.
#
# THREE LAYERS OF ESCAPING
#   &#x20; and &#x7E; are XML character references, expanded by the XML parser,
#     so the IR expression holds a literal SPACE and a literal TILDE.
#   \n and \r are XSD-REGEX escapes, passed through by the XML parser as two
#     characters each, denoting LF and CR to a regex reader.
#   The generated constructor receives DECODED text: an actual U+000A.
#
# THE CHARACTER CLASS
# [ -~\n\r] is U+0020 SPACE .. U+007E TILDE, PLUS U+000A and U+000D. It excludes
# TAB, U+000B, U+000C, NUL, every other C0 control, DEL (U+007F), and every
# non-ASCII character. The cases below pin all the boundaries.
#
# NORMALIZATION APPLIES FIRST
# whiteSpace = collapse (XML Schema Part 2 4.3.6) runs BEFORE the pattern and
# length facets. Consequences tested below:
#   - a RAW input longer than 1024 is VALID when its NORMALIZED form fits;
#   - TAB, LF, and CR become SPACE, so they never reach the class test;
#   - leading and trailing runs are removed, interior runs become ONE space;
#   - only XML's FOUR whitespace characters participate. U+00A0 and every other
#     Unicode space are ordinary characters, and are REJECTED by the class test
#     rather than normalized away. Invalid controls are never silently deleted.
#
# LENGTH IS A CHARACTER COUNT
# Every accepted character is at most U+007E, hence single-byte in UTF-8, so the
# UTF-8 byte count equals the XSD character count for this alphabet.
#
# BOUNDS
# This corpus is written for the 0..1024 member.

# --- VALID: the empty and whitespace-only values ---
# minLength = 0, so the empty string is a VALID value of this type.
VALID <empty> => <empty>
# Whitespace-only input NORMALIZES to empty, which then fits minLength 0.
VALID \s => <empty>
VALID \s\s\s => <empty>
VALID \t => <empty>
VALID \n => <empty>
VALID \r => <empty>
VALID \t\n\r\s => <empty>
VALID \n\n\n => <empty>

# --- VALID: the class boundaries themselves ---
VALID ~ => ~
VALID ! => !
VALID } => }
VALID | => |
VALID 0 => 0
VALID 9 => 9
VALID A => A
VALID z => z
# A lone SPACE is whitespace, so it normalizes away; see above.

# --- VALID: leading and trailing runs are REMOVED ---
VALID \sabc => abc
VALID abc\s => abc
VALID \s\s\sabc\s\s\s => abc
VALID \tabc\t => abc
VALID \nabc\r => abc

# --- VALID: interior runs collapse to exactly ONE space ---
VALID a\sb => a\sb
VALID a\s\sb => a\sb
VALID a\s\s\s\s\sb => a\sb
VALID a\tb => a\sb
VALID a\nb => a\sb
VALID a\rb => a\sb
VALID a\t\n\rb => a\sb
VALID a\s\tb => a\sb
VALID \s\sa\s\s\sb\s\s => a\sb

# --- VALID: normalization is IDEMPOTENT ---
# Each expected form below is itself a valid input that maps to itself.
VALID a\sb\sc => a\sb\sc
VALID hello\sworld => hello\sworld

# --- VALID: ordinary words and punctuation ---
VALID hello => hello
VALID Callsign-7 => Callsign-7
VALID a,b.c;d:e!f?g => a,b.c;d:e!f?g
VALID {a|b}~c => {a|b}~c
VALID \s\sTOP\sSECRET\s\s => TOP\sSECRET

# --- INVALID: characters OUTSIDE the class, never silently deleted ---
# NUL. An empty stored value and a NUL character are different things.
INVALID \u{0}
INVALID a\u{0}b
# VERTICAL TAB and FORM FEED are NOT XML whitespace and NOT in the class.
INVALID \u{b}
INVALID a\u{b}b
INVALID \u{c}
INVALID a\u{c}b
# U+001F, immediately below SPACE.
INVALID \u{1f}
INVALID a\u{1f}b
# DEL, immediately above TILDE.
INVALID \u{7f}
INVALID a\u{7f}b
# NO-BREAK SPACE and other non-ASCII whitespace are NOT XML whitespace, so they
# are not normalized; they reach the class test and are rejected.
INVALID \u{a0}
INVALID a\u{a0}b
INVALID a\u{2028}b
INVALID a\u{3000}b
# Non-ASCII letters and multibyte characters.
INVALID caf\u{e9}
INVALID \u{5e74}
INVALID a\u{1f600}b
